name: Chelmsford
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Chelmsford, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Chelmsford, MA: the Holiday Prelude and tree lighting with Santa and hayrides, a gingerbread village, and trains near Lowell.
lede: Chelmsford celebrates Christmas with a Sunday Holiday Prelude on the Town Common, full of hayrides, music and Santa, and with a church gingerbread village built by local kids and grownups.
celebrates: Chelmsford's biggest Christmas tradition is the Holiday Prelude and Tree Lighting on the Town Common, held on the first Sunday in December and run by the Holiday Decorating Committee, a group of volunteers appointed by the town manager. Families enjoy music, treats, story times, face painting, horse drawn hayrides and tractor rides while they wait for Santa, and most activities are free. North Chelmsford holds its own tree lighting on the Vinal Square common, with Santa arriving by fire truck. At All Saints' Episcopal Church, kids and adults build gingerbread houses for a Gingerbread Village that the public can tour.
lastyear: In 2025 the town held its Annual Holiday Prelude and Tree Lighting on Chelmsford Common on Sunday, December 7, from 4 to 6 pm. Santa arrived at 4 pm, the tree was lit at 5 pm, and families enjoyed free goodies, hayrides, face painting and live performances on the Common. Age Friendly Chelmsford and Chelmsford TV helped spread the word about the Prelude ahead of the day, and the evening drew families from all over town to the Common.
facts: Chelmsford was founded in 1652 by settlers from Woburn and Concord and was incorporated in May 1655, named after Chelmsford in England. The farming area of East Chelmsford later became the city of Lowell in the 1820s, one of the first large factory towns in the country. Both the Middlesex Canal and the Middlesex Turnpike were built through Chelmsford in the early 1800s, long before cars.
trains: The Stony Brook Railroad opened on July 4, 1848, a 13.19 mile line from Lowell through Chelmsford and Westford toward Ayer, with stops including West Chelmsford, Graniteville and Forge Village. Today Chelmsford has no passenger station of its own, but LRTA buses 15, 16 and 17 connect the town to Lowell station on the MBTA Commuter Rail Lowell Line for a holiday trip into Boston. For a Christmas train through the lights, Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train.

kidfact: Chelmsford is older than its big neighbor Lowell. Lowell used to be a farming part of Chelmsford called East Chelmsford before it became its own town in the 1820s.
faq: When is the Chelmsford tree lighting?

Chelmsford holds its Holiday Prelude and Tree Lighting on the Town Common on the first Sunday in December, from 4 to 6 pm, with the tree lit at 5 pm. In 2025 that was Sunday, December 7, and Santa arrived at 4 pm. The town's Holiday Decorating Committee organizes the whole event.
Is the Chelmsford Holiday Prelude free?

The town's flyer says admission to most of the events is free and donations are appreciated. Families can expect hayrides, free goodies, face painting, performances and a visit from Santa. Since the flyer says most activities rather than all of them, it helps to bring a little cash for donations.
What is the All Saints' Gingerbread Village?

All Saints' Episcopal Church at 10 Billerica Road invites kids and adults to build gingerbread houses, which are shown to the public for one day in early December. The church suggests a donation per family to visit, and donated houses are raffled to support the church's outreach groups.
How do you get from Chelmsford to Boston by train?

Chelmsford has no commuter rail station of its own. LRTA bus routes 15, 16 and 17 run from Chelmsford to Lowell station, a stop on the MBTA Commuter Rail Lowell Line, where trains head into Boston. North Billerica station on the same line is another nearby stop for a holiday day trip.
